subject: Local Integrator Connector Program — compliance handoff & packaging
messages:
From: Sophie Dubois <sophie.dubois@eurointegrate.fr>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kai Mori <kai.mori@tsumugi-consulting.jp>
Date: 2027-04-28T08:12:00Z
Subject: Local integrator packaging & GDPR-local hosting question

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at EuroIntegrate is excited about the latency/cost profile you showed. A couple of customers in France and Germany require that any LLM inference for PII stays within-country or at least within the EU.

We want to propose a local integrator offering: EuroIntegrate would deploy Redwood-managed connectors into customer VPCs (or on-prem enclaves) and provide first-level ops. Before we put this in a partner SOW, can you share a short spec of the connector (network ports, data-at-rest controls, expected kernel/response characteristics) and any packaging constraints we should be aware of?

Also: are there existing deployment artifacts (Ansible/helm/docker images) that simplify an integrator-facing playbook?

I've attached a one-page requirements brief (attachment: eu_local_requirements.pdf) for context. Looking to align on what Redwood can support out-of-the-box versus what we'd white-label.

Best,
Sophie
Partnerships Director
EuroIntegrate

---
Attachment: eu_local_requirements.pdf (1 page, summary)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Dubois <sophie.dubois@eurointegrate.fr>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Local integrator packaging & GDPR-local hosting question

Hi Sophie — really appreciate the brief and the clear ask. Short answers up-front: yes, we support an integrator-managed deployment model and we have a connector spec that lists network, KMS, and storage requirements. We also have a lightweight helm chart and prebuilt OCI images for the connector layer.

I'm attaching the connector spec (connector_specs_v1.pdf) and a draft packaging checklist (redwood-eu-packaging.xlsx) so you can map to EuroIntegrate's delivery model. Key callouts:
- Our recommended mode for EU customers is VPC-hosted connector + optional KV cache on local NVMe.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS/HSM) and a transient key approach for caching.
- Audit logs: we can ship structured logs to customer SIEM or keep an isolated audit bucket — both are supported but differ on retention/export guarantees.

Next step: can we set a technical handoff meeting (30–45m) that includes your lead integrator and our infra engineering? If yes, please propose times.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Partner GTM, Redwood Inference
Attachments: connector_specs_v1.pdf; redwood-eu-packaging.xlsx

Date: 2027-04-30T14:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Local integrator packaging & GDPR-local hosting question

Ben / Lauren / Sophie — thanks for the context. Quick engineering summary and commitments we can make for the pilot:

1) Deployables: we will provide the connector as an OCI image plus helm chart. We'll deliver an Ansible wrapper for sites without Helm. Attachment: managed_onprem_guide.docx (install + rollback runbook).
2) Security: customer KMS required for production; for pilot we can accept Redwood-managed keys behind an NDA. Full SOC2 artifact pack can be provided on request.
3) Observability: we can add an integrator-specific tag in tracing and provide a dashboard export (CSV). We will expose token-level latency/cost per-route to partner console.
4) SLA: for integrator-support pilots we recommend a 24x5 support window with a 4-hour P1 response SLA. Full 24x7 is possible with a premium support add-on.

Next steps:
- I'll open a JIRA to track integration tasks (INFR-3245).
- Ben, Lauren: if commercial terms look OK, we can produce a scoped SOW and a DocuSign-ready SOW template.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Infrastructure Engineering
Attachments: managed_onprem_guide.docx
